title: Outlook for Mac: Purview DLP wait-on-send support
summary: Hold: the DLP rule creation command omits a required matching condition, and the timeout discussion omits the documented configuration that prevents Send anyway. The roadmap details and the distinction between planned Mac support and documented Windows controls are otherwise supported.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; controls notes; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn does not yet document Mac wait-on-send configuration or tie the Windows controls to Mac.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send DLP DLPWaitOnSendEnabled licensing default timeout; "Outlook for Mac" "wait-on-send". Read mobile and Windows policy-tip references, oversharing setup and Set-OrganizationConfig; none documents a Mac setting or Mac applicability.

claims.claim: Outlook for Microsoft 365 wait on send can be configured through the dlpwaitonsendtimeout registry key.
claims.quote: Optionally, you can set the *dlpwaitonsendtimeout Regkey (Value in dword)* on all the devices where you want to implement "wait on send" for oversharing pop-ups.

claims.claim: The corresponding Group Policy setting is Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content.
claims.quote: You can set this *RegKey* via group policy, **Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content**, script, or other mechanism for configuring registry keys.

claims.claim: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled and DLPWaitOnSendTimeout control wait to send in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: The wait-to-send experience is controlled solely through the following Exchange mailbox parameters:

claims.claim: The mobile/macOS reference's wait-on-send section says Android and iOS, not macOS, do not yet support it.
claims.quote: Outlook for Android and iOS doesn't yet support *DLP Wait-to-Send, which is* centrally managed

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, when wait on send is not configured, Send sends immediately.
claims.quote: When *dlpwaitonsendtimeout* isn't configured, the message isn't checked before the user sends it. The email message is sent immediately once **Send** is clicked.

claims.claim: In that unconfigured Outlook for Microsoft 365 case, DLP evaluation and policy actions occur afterwards.
claims.quote: The email message is sent immediately once **Send** is clicked. The DLP data classification service evaluates the message and apply the actions defined in the DLP policy.

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, an unfinished evaluation after the timeout presents Send anyway, without stating the no-override configuration.
claims.quote: If the **T** value is greater than 9999, it's replaced with 10000 and the **Send Anyway** button doesn't appear. This holds the message until the policy evaluation completes and doesn't provide the user with an *override* option.
claims.fix: Replace the opening and Outlook for Microsoft 365 clauses with: 'On other clients, some timeout configurations allow a bypass. For Outlook for Microsoft 365, a configured wait of 0 to 9999 seconds offers Send anyway if evaluation has not completed; values above 9999 are replaced with 10000 and hold the message until evaluation completes without an override.' Retain the separate new Outlook timeout-of-0 example. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-osp-get-started.

claims.claim: In new Outlook for Windows, a timeout of 0 shows Send Anyway immediately.
claims.quote: When DLPWaitOnSendTimeout = 0, user will immediately see “Send Anyway” in the infobar of mail.

claims.claim: Learn says matched DLP block rules block the message regardless of Policy tips configuration.
claims.quote: If the block rules defined in the DLP policy are met, the message will be blocked regardless of how **Policy tips** is configured.

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, evaluation duration varies with internet speed, content length and policy count.
claims.quote: The duration for completing the evaluation can vary depending on factors such as internet speed, content length, and the number of policies defined.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <DLP Rule Name> -Policy <DLP Policy Name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog" is a runnable rule-creation call.

Replace it with the complete warn-rule example from the existing cited source: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <DLP Rule Name> -Policy <DLP Policy Name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @(@{operator = "And"; groups = @(@{operator="Or";name="Default";labels=@(@{name=<Label GUID>;type="Sensitivity"})})}) -ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs @("contoso.com","microsoft.com").
